claim: There exist integer partitions lam, mu, nu, each of length at most 7 and of size at most 30, with |lam| = |mu| + |nu|, such that the stretched Littlewood-Richardson polynomial P(t) = c^{t lam}_{t mu, t nu} (a polynomial in t by Derksen-Weyman 2002) has at least one negative coefficient in the monomial basis 1, t, t^2, ...

quadruple.statement: There exist integer partitions lam, mu, nu, each of length at most 7 and of size at most 30, with |lam| = |mu| + |nu|, such that the stretched Littlewood-Richardson polynomial P(t) = c^{t lam}_{t mu, t nu} (a polynomial in t by Derksen-Weyman 2002) has at least one negative coefficient in the monomial basis 1, t, t^2, ...
quadruple.stage: Ehrhart theory of the Knutson-Tao hive polytope: for each triple, P(t) is the Ehrhart polynomial of the rational polytope H(lam,mu,nu) in R^D, D = dim H <= (n-1)(n-2)/2 <= 15 for n <= 7 parts, cut out by rhombus inequalities with 0/+-1 normals; the claim is a finite search over the finite set of triples in the box (length <= 7, size <= 30), each instance decided by one exact polytope computation

shape.objects: Triples (lam, mu, nu) of integer partitions with length <= 7, size <= 30, |lam| = |mu| + |nu|: a finite set (of the order of 10^8 triples before symmetry). For each triple the object is the integer-valued polynomial P(t) of degree D = dim H(lam,mu,nu) <= 15 and the rational polytope H itself (integral vertices for <= 4 parts; half-integral and worse vertices occur from 5 parts, largest vertex denominator at 5 parts is 7 per the ktt-positivity audit). The Littlewood-Richardson coefficient is not defined in Mathlib: a GitHub code search of leanprover-community/mathlib4 on 2026-09-03 for LittlewoodRichardson, Littlewood-Richardson, and SchurPolynomial returned nothing; only YoungDiagram and SemistandardYoungTableau exist.
shape.quantifiers: Existential over the finite box of triples, then existential over the coefficient index k in {0,...,D}: exists (lam,mu,nu) in the box, exists k, a_k(lam,mu,nu) < 0. It is the negation of the King-Tollu-Toumazet positivity conjecture restricted to the box. Per triple it is a decision problem with a finite exact answer; overall it is a finite search.
shape.target_quantity: Existence, decided by exhibiting one triple with a certified negative coefficient: the triple, its polynomial, and the index k. No constant, exponent, density, or threshold is asked for.
shape.ambient_structure: Three kinds of structure coexist: (i) representation theory / symmetric functions (c^{lam}_{mu nu} = multiplicity of s_lam in s_mu s_nu, counted by LR tableaux under the lattice-word rule); (ii) polyhedral geometry (Knutson-Tao 1999: c = number of lattice points of the hive polytope H whose facets are rhombus inequalities with 0/+-1 normals; P(t) is the Ehrhart polynomial of H and deg P = dim H); (iii) the Horn/LR cone (KTT 2009: on a tight Horn facet P factorises as a product of two smaller stretched LR polynomials). The simpler ambient that keeps the constraint is Ehrhart theory of rational polytopes whose facet normals lie in the finite rhombus-normal set N_n of side n (Ferudun 2026, dilation lemma: coefficient signs are those of the lattice polytope qH).
shape.symmetries: c^{lam}_{mu nu} = c^{lam}_{nu mu}; conjugation c^{lam'}_{mu' nu'} = c^{lam}_{mu nu} (exchanges lengths and first parts, keeps sizes); the S_3 symmetry of the triple-product multiplicity with complemented partitions inside a rectangle; column addition c^{lam + (1^n)}_{mu + (1^n), nu} = c^{lam}_{mu nu} for n >= max length (reduces size by n, keeps P). All of these keep P(t). The rhombus-normal set N_n is invariant under the dihedral symmetry of the hive triangle.
shape.configuration: No forbidden configuration; the required configuration is a sign: a_k < 0 for some k in the Ehrhart polynomial of H. Algebraic relations: a_0 = 1, D! a_D = normalized volume > 0, a_{D-1} = half the normalized boundary volume > 0; for a full-dimensional hive the coefficients of t^D, t^{D-1}, t^{D-2}, t^{D-3} are positive, and for a full-dimensional 5-part hive (D = 6) every coefficient but a_1 is positive (Ferudun 2026). The configuration is destroyed by Horn-facet factorisation (a product of two coefficientwise-positive polynomials is positive), so a counterexample is primitive (every Horn inequality strict) or contains a primitive counterexample as a factor.
shape.extremal_candidate: Not applicable (no extremum). Candidate classes named in print: the Chen-Robbins-Yuen polytope case (mu = nu = staircase, lam = 2 x staircase; Epoch problem note: its Ehrhart positivity is unknown), which lies outside the box for 6 or more parts; Reeve-tetrahedron-like polytopes (few lattice points, large volume, lattice-sparse boundary) as the Ehrhart-theoretic shape of a negative linear coefficient; stretched Kostka / skew Gelfand-Tsetlin polytopes are Ehrhart positive (Jochemko-Menon 2026) and so are not a source.
shape.finite_certificates: The true side has a finite certificate: one triple with its polynomial computed exactly (Normaliz Ehrhart series from the rhombus inequalities, or D+1 exact lattice-point counts with Newton interpolation and held-out dilations) and an index k with a_k < 0, re-checkable by an independent Littlewood-Richardson counter (lattice-word rule, lrcalc) at small t and by exact rational interpolation. The false side (no counterexample in the box) is finite in principle but its certificate is an exhaustive computation over about 10^8 triples with polynomials of degree up to 15, beyond current reach (Epoch note: 'hard going past length 6 or so').
shape.monotonicity: Monotone in the box: a counterexample within (length <= 7, size <= 30) is one within every larger box; the search runs by increasing size bound N and number of parts n. No counterexample is known at any (n, N): Ferudun 2026 reports extensive computation with none, and the ktt-positivity repository reports a search of about 4 x 10^8 triples with none (ranges not recorded). Smallest open number of parts: n = 5 (n <= 4 is proved positive); within 5 parts the only open coefficient of a full-dimensional hive is a_1, and lower-dimensional 5-part hives of dimension >= 3 are open in every coefficient below the top four.
shape.uniformity_parameter: The number of parts n: D = (n-1)(n-2)/2 grows quadratically (D <= 6, 10, 15 for n = 5, 6, 7) and the cost of one exact Ehrhart polynomial grows with D; n = 5 is cheap, n = 6 moderate, n = 7 is the edge of the box and of published computation. The size bound N = 30 fixes the number of instances.
shape.proof_shape: A finite computation per instance: (1) fix a triple; (2) compute dim H and the Ehrhart polynomial of H exactly (Normaliz from the rhombus inequalities, as LattE was used by De Loera-McAllister 2006, or D+1 exact lattice-point counts plus Newton interpolation with two held-out dilations, as KTT 2006 and Ferudun 2026 did); (3) read the sign of every coefficient; (4) certify by an independent counter and an independent interpolation. Loss per step: none (exact arithmetic). The search over triples has no argument, only heuristics (small c with large volume, primitive triples, lattice-sparse boundary). A standard solver (Normaliz, LattE) runs the finite step; a proof assistant does not, because Mathlib has no Littlewood-Richardson coefficient.
shape.neighbours: (1) KTT positivity for length <= 4: known true (Ferudun 2026, arXiv:2607.22301, computer-assisted, replay scripts at github.com/AlperTheKing/ktt-positivity). (2) c = 1 implies P = 1: known true (Knutson-Tao-Woodward 2004); c = 2 implies P = t + 1: known true (Ikenmeyer 2016; Sherman 2017). (3) Polynomiality of P: known true (Derksen-Weyman 2002; Rassart 2004; Thawinrak 2022). (4) Top four coefficients of every full-dimensional hive positive, and full-dimensional 5-part hives positive except possibly a_1: known true (Ferudun 2026). (5) Ehrhart positivity for general lattice polytopes: known false (Reeve tetrahedra; Castillo et al., 'Smooth polytopes with negative Ehrhart coefficients', JCTA 160 (2018), arXiv:1704.05532; Liu-Tsuchiya, 'Stanley's non-Ehrhart-positive order polytopes', 2019, arXiv:1806.08403; Ferroni-Higashitani survey, EMS Surv. Math. Sci. 2024). (6) Ehrhart positivity of skew Gelfand-Tsetlin and marked order polytopes (stretched Kostka): known true (Jochemko-Menon 2026, arXiv:2604.08394). (7) The 3 x 8 transportation-polytope transfer into LR: valid but the family is Ehrhart positive (ktt-positivity, ORDER_TRANSFER_3ROW_VERDICT.md): no negative input. (8) Stretched Newell-Littlewood coefficients: quasi-polynomial of period <= 2, positivity conjectured (King 2021, arXiv:2101.00984): open. (9) Saturation fails for Schubert coefficients (arXiv:2601.04182): known, a different object. (10) The full KTT conjecture: open; the Epoch AI FrontierMath open problem is this claim with the box added for verifiability, and its author expects the conjecture to be false.
shape.known_bounds: Positive side (where no counterexample can be): length <= 4, every triple (theorem); c <= 2 (theorem); full-dimensional 5-part hives, coefficients a_2..a_6 (theorem), a_1 open; 'extensive computation has produced no counterexample' (Ferudun 2026) and a search of about 4 x 10^8 triples with none (ktt-positivity GENERALIZATION_REPORT.md, ranges unrecorded); De Loera-McAllister 2006 computed stretched LR polynomials with LattE at small rank and found no negative coefficient (their Conjecture 4.7 restates positivity). Negative side: nothing. Documented ceilings: exhaustive coverage of the box is out of reach (Epoch note: hard past 6 parts); the direct method costs one exact Ehrhart computation per triple (this workspace, tools/hivepoly.py: milliseconds at D <= 6, to be measured at D = 10..15); the 3 x 8 transportation transfer family has minimum linear coefficient 2157/280 > 0; on the proof side termwise Berline-Vergne positivity fails at codimension 4 (a cell of weight -349/28800) and the general conjecture reduces to an unproved hive-specific effectivity statement (HTE).
shape.missing_input: For the negative side: one triple; no argument in print locates one, and the only guidance is Ehrhart-theoretic (negative coefficients come from h*-mass at high index: few lattice points at small dilations against a large volume). For the positive side: (HTE) of Ferudun 2026.
shape.base_theory: ZFC. Every instance is a finite integer computation (lattice-point counts of a rational polytope, exact rational interpolation), decidable and provable in Peano arithmetic; the machine check (Normaliz's exact arithmetic, Python integers and Fractions) stays inside the base theory; no hypothesis beyond ZFC bears on the claim or on any neighbour. A Lean check would first need a definition of the hive count or of LR coefficients, absent from Mathlib on 2026-09-03.

known: P(t) = c^{t lam}_{t mu, t nu} is a polynomial in t: Derksen and Weyman, J. Algebra 255 (2002) 247-257, doi:10.1016/S0021-8693(02)00125-4; Rassart, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 107 (2004) 161-179, arXiv:math/0308101; Thawinrak, arXiv:2211.06810.
c = number of integer hives (lattice points of the hive polytope), and saturation: Knutson and Tao, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 12 (1999) 1055-1090.

The positivity conjecture (every coefficient of P nonnegative), with the polynomial nature and factorisation on Horn facets: King, Tollu, Toumazet, CRM Proc. Lecture Notes 34 (2004) 99-112, doi:10.1090/crmp/034/10 (zbMATH 2124855); Sem. Lothar. Combin. 54A (2006) B54Ad (zbMATH 5660467); J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 116 (2009) 314-333, doi:10.1016/j.jcta.2008.06.005.
c = 1 implies P = 1: Knutson, Tao, Woodward, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 17 (2004) 19-48.
c = 2 implies P = t + 1: Ikenmeyer, J. Algebraic Combin. 44 (2016) 1-29, arXiv:1209.1521; Sherman, arXiv:1505.06551 and J. Algebra (2017) doi:10.1016/j.jalgebra.2017.03.011.
Computed stretched LR polynomials with LattE, all with nonnegative coefficients; positivity restated as Conjecture 4.7: De Loera and McAllister, Experiment. Math. 15 (2006), arXiv:math/0501446.
Number of LR tableaux weakly increases when the shape and content of another LR tableau are added: Gutschwager, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 118 (2011), doi:10.1016/j.jcta.2011.02.005, arXiv:0904.4778.

Positivity for all triples of length <= 4; top four coefficients of every full-dimensional hive positive; full-dimensional 5-part hives positive except possibly the linear coefficient; the general conjecture reduced to the effectivity statement (HTE); the 3 x 8 transportation transfer is Ehrhart positive; extensive computation and a ~4 x 10^8-triple search found no counterexample: Ferudun, arXiv:2607.22301 (2026-07-24) and github.com/AlperTheKing/ktt-positivity (cloned 2026-09-03).

The claim is Epoch AI's FrontierMath open problem 'Stretched Littlewood-Richardson coefficients' (https://epoch.ai/frontiermath/open-problems/stretched-lr-coefficients, background PDF read 2026-09-03): the author expects the conjecture to be false; the box (length <= 7, size <= 30) is for verifiability; the note says search is hard past 6 parts.
Skew Gelfand-Tsetlin and marked order polytopes are Ehrhart positive (so stretched Kostka numbers give no negative coefficient): Jochemko and Menon, arXiv:2604.08394 (2026).

General lattice polytopes are not Ehrhart positive: Reeve tetrahedra (linear coefficient 2 - r/6); Castillo et al., J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 160 (2018) 316-331, arXiv:1704.05532 (smooth polytopes with every possibly-negative coefficient negative); Liu and Tsuchiya, Adv. Appl. Math. 108 (2019), arXiv:1806.08403 (order polytopes).
